author: Kusha N M
raw:
ನೀನೆ ಎನ್ನುತಲಿರಲು ನಾನು ಹೋಗಲೆಬೇಕು
ಸಾಣೆ ಹಿಡಿಯದಿಹ ಮನ ನನ್ನೆ ಹುಡುಕುವುದು
ಆನನದಿ ಬಿಂಬಿಸಿರೆ ನಾನೆ ಎಂಬುವ ಭಾವ
ಕಾಣೆಯಾಗುವೆ ನೀನು ಮೂಢಮನುಜ

lines: To say ‘Thou alone’, the ‘I’ must go;
the mind not honed upon the whetstone seeks only ‘me’;
when ‘I alone’ is written on your face,
the ‘Thou’ is lost from sight, O deluded one.
en.note: The verse turns on nīne (‘you alone’, said to the Divine) and nāne (‘I alone’). The last line can also be read: ‘you yourself will vanish’.
en.bhavartha: To truly say ‘Thou alone’ to the Divine, the ego has to step aside. An unrefined mind keeps looking for ‘me’. And when ‘I alone’ is written all over our face, God slips out of sight; read another way, we ourselves are lost.
